knowledge:
- key_parameters: formula=An expression containing covariates used to adjust the model (e.g., ~Sex+Age) ;; expset=The name of the ExposomeSet in the MultiDataSet object (e.g., "exposures") ;; omicset=The name of the omic-set in the MultiDataSet object (e.g., "expression" or "proteome") ;; sva=Enables Surrogate Variable Analysis; set to "fast" (uses isva and SmartSVA) or "slow" (uses sva) to correct for inflation/deflation ;; method=In association(), sets the fitting method for lmFit ("ls" for least squares, "robust" for robust regression); in crossomics(), sets the integration method ("mcia" for multiple co-inertia analysis, "mcca" for multi canonical correlation analysis) ;; permute=In crossomics() with MCCA, sets internal permutation and iteration parameters for tuning
- alternatives: association() vs crossomics()=Use association() to test pairwise associations between two complete datasets (removing samples with missing values). Use crossomics() to find latent relationships between two or more datasets simultaneously ;; mcia vs mcca=In crossomics(), "mcia" (multiple co-inertia analysis from omicade4) is used for multi-dataset integration, while "mcca" (multi canonical correlation analysis from PMA) is used for canonical correlation-based integration
- when_to_use: Use when you have exposome data (ExposomeSet) and one or more omic datasets (ExpressionSet, MethylationSet, SummarizedExperiment) for the same individuals and want to perform association testing or multi-omic integration.
- pitfalls: Missing values in exposome data can cause issues in integration analysis; users must check for missing values using plotMissings() and perform imputation() before running crossomics() ;; Low lambda scores (under 1) in association models indicate a need for Surrogate Variable Analysis (sva = "fast" or "slow") ;; ResultSet objects generated by crossomics() do not support plotHits(), plotLambda(), or plotAssociation(); use plotIntegration() instead

workflows.name: association_study
workflows.intent: Perform association testing between exposome data and a single omic dataset (e.g., transcriptome or proteome) using a limma-based pipeline with optional SVA adjustment.
workflows.stages: 1. Load exposome and omic datasets ;; 2. Create a MultiDataSet object and add both datasets using createMultiDataSet(), add_genexp() (or add_eset()), and add_exp() ;; 3. Run association analysis using association() ;; 4. Evaluate results using tableHits() and tableLambda() ;; 5. Re-run association with SVA adjustment (sva = "fast") if lambda scores indicate inflation/deflation ;; 6. Visualize associations using plotAssociation() (QQ plots, volcano plots, or protein plots)
workflows.code:
library(omicRexposome)
library(MultiDataSet)
data("brge_expo", package = "brgedata")
data("brge_gexp", package = "brgedata")
mds <- createMultiDataSet()
mds <- add_genexp(mds, brge_gexp)
mds <- add_exp(mds, brge_expo)
gexp <- association(mds, formula=~Sex+Age, expset = "exposures", omicset = "expression")
hit <- tableHits(gexp, th=0.001)
lab <- tableLambda(gexp)
merge(hit, lab, by="exposure")
gexp <- association(mds, formula=~Sex+Age, expset = "exposures", omicset = "expression", sva = "fast")
hit <- tableHits(gexp, th=0.001)
lab <- tableLambda(gexp)
merge(hit, lab, by="exposure")
gridExtra::grid.arrange(
    plotAssociation(gexp, rid="Ben_p", type="qq") + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Transcriptome - Pb Association"),
    plotAssociation(gexp, rid="BPA_p", type="qq") + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Transcriptome - THM Association"),
    ncol=2
)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(
    plotAssociation(gexp, rid="Ben_p", type="volcano", tPV=-log10(1e-04)) + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Transcriptome - Pb Association"),
    plotAssociation(gexp, rid="BPA_p", type="volcano", tPV=-log10(1e-04)) + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Transcriptome - THM Association"),
    ncol=2
)
data("brge_prot", package="brgedata")
mds <- createMultiDataSet()
mds <- add_eset(mds, brge_prot, dataset.type  ="proteome")
mds <- add_exp(mds, brge_expo)
prot <- association(mds, formula=~Sex+Age, expset = "exposures", omicset = "proteome")
tableHits(prot, th=0.001)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(
    plotAssociation(prot, rid="Ben_p", type="protein") + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Proteome - Cd Association") +
        ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "LightPink"),
    plotAssociation(prot, rid="NO2_p", type="protein") + 
        ggplot2::ggtitle("Proteome - Cotinine Association") +
        ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "LightPink"),
    ncol=2
)

workflows.name: integration_analysis
workflows.intent: Integrate multiple datasets (exposome and multiple omics datasets) to find latent relationships using MCIA or MCCA after resolving missing values.
workflows.stages: 1. Load exposome and multiple omic datasets ;; 2. Check for missing values in the exposome dataset using plotMissings() ;; 3. Impute missing values in the exposome dataset using imputation() ;; 4. Create a MultiDataSet object and add all datasets using createMultiDataSet(), add_genexp(), add_eset(), and add_exp() ;; 5. Perform integration analysis using crossomics() with method = "mcia" or method = "mcca" ;; 6. Define colors for visualization ;; 7. Visualize the integrated datasets using plotIntegration()
workflows.code:
library(rexposome)
plotMissings(brge_expo, set = "exposures")
brge_expo <- imputation(brge_expo)
mds <- createMultiDataSet()
mds <- add_genexp(mds, brge_gexp)
mds <- add_eset(mds, brge_prot, dataset.type = "proteome")
mds <- add_exp(mds, brge_expo)
cr_mcia <- crossomics(mds, method = "mcia", verbose = TRUE)
cr_mcia
cr_mcca <- crossomics(mds, method = "mcca", permute=c(4, 2))
cr_mcca
colors <- c("green", "blue", "red")
names(colors) <- names(mds)
plotIntegration(cr_mcia, colors=colors)
plotIntegration(cr_mcca, colors=colors)
